prompt: How many electron pairs are involved in a [1,5] sigmatropic rearrangement?
explanation: A [1,5] sigmatropic rearrangement involves three electron pairs: two π bonds and one σ bond. An odd number of pairs means a thermal suprafacial reaction (Table 30.7.1).

prompt: How does a thermal [1,5] hydrogen shift across two double bonds take place?

choices.why: Three electron pairs is an odd number, and thermal odd-pair rearrangements are suprafacial.

choices.text: It doesn't occur thermally; it needs UV light
choices.why: [1,5] hydrogen shifts are commonly observed thermally; 5-methyl-1,3-cyclopentadiene rearranges at room temperature.
A hydrogen shift is a sigmatropic rearrangement, described as suprafacial or antarafacial.

explanation: With three electron pairs, Table 30.7.1 predicts a suprafacial reaction. The suprafacial [1,5] shift of a hydrogen atom across two double bonds is a commonly observed sigmatropic rearrangement (Figure 30.8.1).

prompt: What happens to 5-methyl-1,3-cyclopentadiene at room temperature?

choices.text: It rapidly rearranges by [1,5] hydrogen shifts to a mixture of the 1-methyl-, 2-methyl- and 5-methyl- isomers
Nothing; [1,5] hydrogen shifts require UV light
choices.why: These suprafacial [1,5] hydrogen shifts are thermal and occur rapidly at room temperature.
A second [1,5] shift turns the 1-methyl isomer into the 2-methyl isomer, and the shifts are reversible, so a mixture results.

choices.text: It opens to a conjugated triene by an electrocyclic reaction
choices.why: The reaction is a sigmatropic hydrogen shift; the ring stays intact.

explanation: 5-Methyl-1,3-cyclopentadiene rapidly rearranges at room temperature by [1,5] hydrogen shifts to give a mixture of 1-methyl-, 2-methyl- and 5-methyl-1,3-cyclopentadiene.

choices.text: Deuterium is scrambled between positions 1 and 5 by a [1,5] shift
Deuterium moves to position 3 by a [1,3] shift
choices.why: Thermal [1,3] hydrogen shifts are unknown; they would need a strained antarafacial path.

choices.text: The diene closes to a deuterated cyclobutene
choices.why: The diene ⇄ cyclobutene equilibrium favors the open-chain diene; the observed change is deuterium scrambling.

choices.text: All the deuterium is lost as D2
choices.why: The deuterium atoms move within the molecule by a sigmatropic shift; none is lost.

explanation: Heating 5,5,5-trideuterio-(3Z)-1,3-pentadiene causes scrambling of deuterium between positions 1 and 5. A deuterium migrates from carbon 5 to carbon 1 by a suprafacial [1,5] shift.

prompt: Why are thermal [1,3] hydrogen shifts unknown?

choices.text: They would have to proceed by a strained antarafacial pathway
They would have to proceed by a suprafacial pathway, which is symmetry-disallowed
choices.why: Suprafacial paths are allowed when the electron count calls for them. A thermal [1,3] shift (two pairs, an even number) would need the antarafacial path.

choices.text: A hydrogen atom can't take part in sigmatropic rearrangements
choices.why: Hydrogen readily migrates in [1,5] shifts.

choices.text: A [1,3] shift involves an odd number of electron pairs
choices.why: A [1,3] shift involves one π bond and one σ bond: two pairs, an even number.

explanation: A [1,3] hydrogen shift involves two electron pairs (one π bond and one σ bond), an even number, so a thermal reaction would have to be antarafacial. That pathway is too strained, and thermal [1,3] hydrogen shifts are unknown.

prompt: Which compounds undergo the Claisen rearrangement?

choices.text: Allyl aryl ethers and allyl vinyl ethers

choices.why: 1,5-Hexadienes undergo the Cope rearrangement to isomeric 1,5-dienes.
Conjugated trienes undergo electrocyclic ring-closure to cyclohexadienes.
A diene and a dienophile undergo the Diels–Alder cycloaddition.

explanation: The Claisen rearrangement acts on either an allyl aryl ether (H2C=CHCH2–O–Ar) or an allyl vinyl ether (H2C=CHCH2–O–CH=CH2). The Cope rearrangement converts a 1,5-hexadiene into an isomeric 1,5-diene.

prompt: In the Claisen rearrangement of allyl phenyl ether, what intermediate isomerizes to o-allylphenol?

choices.text: An allyl cation and a phenoxide ion
choices.why: The Claisen rearrangement is a single pericyclic step; C–O bond breaking and C–C bond making occur at the same time, without ions.
p-Allylphenol is not on the way to the ortho product; it forms only when both ortho positions are blocked (Exercise 30.8.5).
The intermediate keeps two ring C=C bonds; it is a cyclohexadienone that tautomerizes to the aromatic phenol.

explanation: The Claisen rearrangement takes place in a single step through a six-membered cyclic transition state, in which C–O bond breaking and C–C bond making occur simultaneously. The 6-allyl-2,4-cyclohexadienone intermediate then isomerizes to o-allylphenol (Figure 30.8.2).

prompt: How many atoms are in the cyclic transition state of the Claisen rearrangement?
explanation: Like the Diels–Alder reaction, the Claisen rearrangement takes place in a single step through a six-membered cyclic transition state in which bonding electrons reorganize.

prompt: Allyl phenyl ether is labeled with ^14C on the allyl carbon bonded to oxygen. Where is the label in the o-allylphenol product?

choices.text: On the terminal vinylic carbon of the allyl group
On the allyl carbon bonded to the ring
choices.why: The allyl group is transposed: the carbon that was bonded to oxygen ends up at the far end, and the old terminal carbon bonds to the ring.

choices.text: On the middle carbon of the allyl group
choices.why: The middle carbon stays in the middle; the two ends swap roles.

choices.text: On the ring carbon that carries the OH group
choices.why: The labeled carbon belongs to the allyl group and stays in it.

explanation: The rearrangement takes place with transposition of the allyl group: allyl phenyl ether with a ^14C label on the allyl ether carbon gives o-allylphenol with the label on the terminal vinylic carbon. This supports the cyclic, pericyclic mechanism.

prompt: What product would you expect from Claisen rearrangement of 2-butenyl phenyl ether, C6H5–O–CH2CH=CHCH3?

choices.why: That product would need the allyl group to attach through the carbon that was bonded to oxygen. The Claisen rearrangement transposes the allyl unit.
With open ortho positions, the Claisen rearrangement gives the ortho product.
The Claisen rearrangement moves the group to the ring; it doesn't eliminate it.

explanation: Exercise 30.8.4: the new C–C bond forms at the carbon that was at the far end of the allylic group (the CH bearing the methyl), so the product is o-(1-methylallyl)phenol, o-CH(CH3)CH=CH2 on the phenol ring.

prompt: When a 2,6-disubstituted allyl phenyl ether is heated in an attempted Claisen rearrangement, the p-allyl product forms. What two sequential pericyclic reactions explain this?

choices.text: A Claisen rearrangement followed by a Cope rearrangement

choices.why: Hydrogen shifts don't move an allyl group from oxygen to the para carbon.

choices.text: A Diels–Alder reaction followed by a retro-Diels–Alder reaction
choices.why: The answer to Exercise 30.8.5 is two sigmatropic rearrangements, not cycloadditions.

choices.text: An electrocyclic ring-opening followed by ring-closure
choices.why: The allyl group migrates by sigmatropic rearrangements; the ring is not opened.

explanation: Exercise 30.8.5: a Claisen rearrangement moves the allyl group to a blocked ortho carbon, and a Cope rearrangement then carries it on to the para position.

prompt: Heating 1-deuterioindene scrambles the deuterium to all three positions of the five-membered ring. What mechanism accounts for this?

choices.text: A series of thermal [1,3] hydrogen shifts
choices.why: Thermal [1,3] hydrogen shifts are unknown because they would need a strained antarafacial path.
A Claisen rearrangement needs an allyl aryl or allyl vinyl ether.
Thermal [2 + 2] cycloadditions are not observed, and the reaction moves a hydrogen, not two alkenes.

explanation: Exercise 30.8.3: a series of [1,5] hydrogen shifts moves the deuterium around the five-membered ring, just as [1,5] shifts scramble the methyl isomers of methylcyclopentadiene.

prompt: 1,5-Hexadien-3-ol (CH2=CHCH(OH)CH2CH=CH2) is treated with potassium hydride (KH), and the product is then treated with aqueous acid. What is the final product?

choices.text: 1,5-Hexadien-1-ol, an enol, as the stable final product
choices.why: The Cope rearrangement does give an enol after protonation, but it tautomerizes to an aldehyde.
KH is a strong base that makes the oxyanion; it does not oxidize the alcohol to a ketone.
The oxyanion formed by KH undergoes a Cope rearrangement before the acid workup.

explanation: In the oxy-Cope rearrangement, KH converts the alcohol into an oxyanion, a Cope rearrangement follows, and aqueous acid gives an enol that tautomerizes to an aldehyde, 5-hexenal (CH2=CHCH2CH2CH2CHO).

prompt: What is the product of Cope rearrangement of (E)-1,5-heptadiene, CH2=CHCH2CH2CH=CHCH3?

choices.why: The methyl ends up on the carbon that forms the new σ bond, which is carbon 3 of the product, not carbon 2.
A Cope rearrangement converts a 1,5-diene into an isomeric 1,5-diene, not a conjugated diene.
A Cope product is a 1,5-diene; this name has the double bonds at 1 and 4.

explanation: In the [3,3] Cope rearrangement the σ bond between carbons 3 and 4 breaks and a new σ bond forms between carbons 1 and 6, while the π bonds shift. Carbon 6, which carries the methyl group, becomes bonded to carbon 1, giving CH2=CHCH2CH(CH3)CH=CH2, 3-methyl-1,5-hexadiene.

prompt: In bacterial biosynthesis of phenylalanine, which step is a Claisen rearrangement?

choices.why: That step is a decarboxylation.
That step is a reductive amination, the reverse of transamination.
The pathway runs toward phenylalanine; prephenate is made from chorismate.

explanation: Phenylalanine arises from chorismate through a Claisen rearrangement to prephenate, followed by decarboxylation to phenylpyruvate and reductive amination (Figure 30.8.4).
